characters.name: Anthony
characters.description: The oldest of the Bridgerton siblings. Anthony has inherited his late father’s title and responsibilities as head of the family. Nonetheless, he's not eager to wed, struggling between doing his duties and following his own desires. He is the protagonist of the second season. Adaptational Nice Guy: Book Anthony has a volatile temper and can be controlling, aggressive and cold towards Kate, feeling entitled to have his way with her as a husband. He complains about his "marital rights" being denied when Kate says she's not ready to consummate the marriage on their wedding night. Prior to this, he (albeit accidentally) kicks Kate in the stomach as she hides under the desk while he's trying to talk to Maria (Siena). Show Anthony cares about Kate's comfort and consent when going intimate, and henevergets aggressive with or physically hurts her.Furthermore, show Anthony stops being a rake when he meets Kate – in fact, their first meeting takes place after the last time he engages in that behaviour (onscreen) in season 2 episode 1, whereas his rakishness continues well into book 2. Furthermore, show Anthony stops being a rake when he meets Kate – in fact, their first meeting takes place after the last time he engages in that behaviour (onscreen) in season 2 episode 1, whereas his rakishness continues well into book 2. Adaptational Villainy: Perhaps 'Villain' is a bit strong considering hisCharacter Development, but he shows some chauvinistic attitudes, particularly in the first season regarding Daphne's debut season, whereas in book 1, he largely stays out of it and doesn't attempt to make decisions for her. Book Daphne's inability to find a match is attributed to her being "too friendly" (meaning men see her as friend rather than wife-material) as opposed to her brother scaring all of the quality suitors off like he does in the show. Anger Born of Worry: His frequent method of showing concern to anyone he cares about; both his family and hisLove Interest.

characters.name: Benedict
characters.description: The second oldest of the Bridgerton siblings and protagonist of the fourth season. He has a fondness for art and is trying to find his way. Adaptational Personality Change: In the books. Benedict is largelyOut of FocusuntilAn Offer from a Gentleman. In the show, he gets more screen time in the first few seasons, where he starts off more comedic, fun-loving, and relaxed and is introduced to the world of the bohemian and unconventional. Adaptational Sexuality: After seemingAmbiguously Biin season 1, as of season 3, he canonically has relations with both women and men, whereas he does not in the books.Word of Goddescribes him as pansexual. Beware the Nice Ones: He is rarely seen angry, but when it comes to his beloved family andLove Interest, he could suddenly snap. Notable example: When he confronts Philip Cavender for nearly sexually assaulting Sophie and when helping his sister, Francesca, dealing with the solicitor Walter Dundas about her possible pregnancy. Big Brother Instinct:Shares a particularly close bond with his sister Eloise, who, like him, chafes at the expectations of their lives in society.In season 4,following John's death, a solicitor of the Crown insists Francesca must go through a highly invasive examination to confirm whether or not she is pregnant. Benedict is so enraged by the man's lack of empathy towards his grieving sister that he screams at him and looks nearly ready to physically throw him out of the house.

characters.name: Colin
characters.description: The third oldest of the Bridgerton siblings, a kind and naive young man oblivious to the affections of Penelope Featherington. He leads the third season. Adaptational Context Change: His comment about never wanting to court Penelope doesn't come across as badly in the books as on the show. In the books, he impulsively says it to get his brothers off his back rather than in a disparaging comment to a group of young bachelors. In addition, because more time elapses in the books, it happened a long time ago when Colin was much younger than he is by book four. Adaptational Dumbass: Book Colin is socially aware anda matchmaker of sortsfor his siblings, giving them sound advice — he is only lost and clueless when it comes to his own life. However in the show, he is more generally oblivious, plus he nearly falls for at least two scams. Adaptational Nice Guy: Colin in the books has a serious temper, which he directs at Penelope. When angry overLady Whistledown, he grabs Penelope by the arm tight enough to bruise her and make her fall to the ground. It's also worth noting that book Colin doesn't hateWhistledown for any personal slights, but because he's jealous that Penelope has forged a successful writing career, so his anger feels over the top. Show Colin is not aggressive at all, and his anger at Lady Whistledown much more justified by her writings about his family. Adaptational Personality Change: In the books, Colin has a cheeky persona to hide his insecurities and feelings of being lost. In the show, this persona has worn off early by season 2 (after the Marina scandal), making him seem more dour than his book counterpart. The show attempts more of a rakish persona in season 3. In addition, book Colin is more involved in his siblings' lives.

characters.name: Daphne
characters.description: The fourth oldest of the Bridgerton siblings, and the oldest daughter, Daphne is a proper Regency lady in training. She is the debutante heroine of the show's first season season, during which she is trying to find a good match. Adaptational Attractiveness: Book Daphne is far from ugly — none of the Bridgertons are — but Simon initially describes her as an unconventional beauty. This Daphne is the very image of the Regency belle, and is acknowledged as such by everyone around her. Adaptation Dye-Job: In the books, all of the Bridgerton siblings have brown hair. In the show, Daphne's hair is redder and lighter, more of a strawberry blonde. Affectionate Nickname: Her siblings occasionally call her "Daph". Age Lift: Daphne is on her third season inThe Duke and I, making her 21. In the show, she's a debutante, which, unless she was held back, would imply she's about 18 in season 1. In season 2, she states she is 9 years younger than Anthony, who is 29 at that point.

characters.name: Eloise
characters.description: The fifth of the Bridgerton siblings, an inquisitive girl who is not interested in being a lady. Aborted Arc: Season 3 ends with Eloise setting off hand-in-hand with Michaela to join Francesca and John in Scotland, this being her first time travelling anywhere that isn't London/Kent. However, this doesn't really go anywhere – she returns at the start of season 4 with little more to say than there weren't enough people. Her new friendship with Michaela also seems to be forgotten about. Adaptation Personality Change: Of theAdaptational Jerkassvariety. While book Eloise is very much aSpirited Young Lady, who doesn’t marry until her late twenties because of her refusal to settle for less than she deserves, the show plays up her distaste for the marriage mart, to the point she’s disdainful of other women who have the goal of marrying and having a family. In the books, she has a much sweeter disposition, knows how to behave at social gatherings and her feminist inclinations are more subdued. In short, the show emphasizes certain traits of Eloise to turn her into a foil to Daphne, with whom she seems to have a less tumultuous relationship in the novels. Affectionate Nickname: Her siblings sometimes call her "El". "All Grown Up" Remark:Subverted. While Violet certainly thinks that Eloise looks stunning when it's her season, her siblings try not to laugh when she has to wear a large feathered headdress as all the debutantes are ordered to wear in the queen's presence. Eloise herself thinks she looks ridiculous and wonders if she can find a way to get out of it. Her later outfits are nicer, but she still looks more like a kid than aProper Lady— and Eloise is well-aware of it.

characters.name: Francesca
characters.description: The sixth of the Bridgerton siblings, a quiet girl who loves playing piano. After spending the first two seasons away, she makes her debut into society in the third. Adaptational Personality Change: Book Francesca is introverted, but she's not sotimid. In fact, she's arguably the most quietly confident of her sisters (and the only one who becomes her season's incomparable). She also bribes the maids to teach her sex education and has cheeky, forward side, which sets her apart from the archetypal female leads in the series. So far, this element of Francesca's personality is absent in the show. Adaptational Sexuality: As of season 3, she is portrayed asAmbiguously Bi, seeminglyHappily Marriedto John Stirling while also being thrown off by his cousinMichaela. Affectionate Nickname: She is sometimes referred to as Fran or Frannie. Ascended Extra: She goes from aLiving Propin seasons one and two to being the focus of a major subplot (making her debut and becoming a lady wife) in season three and four.

characters.name: Gregory
characters.description: The seventh of the Bridgerton siblings and the youngest son. Annoying Younger Sibling: Particularly to his sisters, especially Hyacinth. At one point he even steals a piece of cake off of Anthony's plate while the Viscount is reading the newspaper. The Baby of the Bunch: He's a child and treated as such. He and Hyacinth often act as a pair, doing childlike things like playing with marbles. Boarding School: Attends Eton causing Gregory to absent for parts of the story. The Dutiful Son: A variant, of the Bridgerton brothers, Gregory seems to be the most eager to enter the marriage mart in search of a love match as Violet has always wanted for her children.

characters.name: Hyacinth
characters.description: Adorably Precocious Child: Shows signs of being quiteperceptive/intuitive, asking about the Duke for Daphne and "Miss Edwina's sister" for Anthony before anyone else does. In season 3, she's the only one who seems to understand that Francesca and Johnenjoysilence. In addition, Hyacinth is shown to be good at card games in season 3, easily beating her brothers. Ascended Extra: She starts getting more screen time in season 4. The Baby of the Bunch: The baby sister and treated as such. She and Gregory often act in tandem as the two youngest of the family. Big Little Sister: For a while, she's taller than her older brother Gregory, which she lords over him. He gets a growth spurt eventually, though. Character Shilling: She engages in a bit of this towards her siblings' love interests, butespeciallytowards Penelope, gushing over herbetrothalto Colin and the idea of becomingsister-in-laws, despitenot interactingonscreen prior to this moment.

characters.name: Violet
characters.description: The Dowager Viscountess Bridgerton, and loving matriarch of the Bridgerton family. Calling the Old Man Out:Daphne calls her out in season one over not actually explaining how sex works and not properly preparing her for married lifeorgiving her a realistic idea about conception.In season two, she attempts to use her happy marriage to Edmund to convince Anthony to marry for love: he retorts that her marriage to his father is the exact reason for his decision, as he saw how Violet's grief at losing Edmund almost destroyed her, and he refuses to cause pain like that to his wife.In season three, it's Francesca's turn as she points out Violet is not very supportive of Francesca's partner of choise because their relationship doesn't conform to Violet's notions of a dramatic, sweeping, all-consuming passion. Daphne calls her out in season one over not actually explaining how sex works and not properly preparing her for married lifeorgiving her a realistic idea about conception. In season two, she attempts to use her happy marriage to Edmund to convince Anthony to marry for love: he retorts that her marriage to his father is the exact reason for his decision, as he saw how Violet's grief at losing Edmund almost destroyed her, and he refuses to cause pain like that to his wife. In season three, it's Francesca's turn as she points out Violet is not very supportive of Francesca's partner of choise because their relationship doesn't conform to Violet's notions of a dramatic, sweeping, all-consuming passion.

characters.name: Edmund
characters.description: The previous viscount, a good husband and father deeply missed by his family. He died suddenly about a decade prior to the start of the show. Deceased Parents Are the Best: The family, particularly Violet and Anthony, look up to Edmund and idolise him. The irony is that in his flashback, the piece of advice he gives Anthony is "you cannot show someone your best without allowing them to see your worst", indicating he probably didn't see himself as so perfect. Died in Your Arms Tonight: Edmund Bridgerton died from being stung by a bee as he and Anthony were collecting flowers, suffering an allergic reaction. He went into anaphylactic shock, as his wife and son were powerless to help him. The only thing a distraught Violet could do was hold her beloved husband as he died. Dies Differently in Adaptation: His cause of death is the same (bee sting), but in the show continuity it's Anthony, not Eloise, who witnesses it. This adds further context to Anthony's trauma and his business-like attitude to finding a wife. Family Man: He was a loving husband and father that his wife and children remember him fondly.

characters.name: Mrs. Wilson
characters.description: The Bridgertons' loyal housekeeper. The Confidant: Violet trusts her with a lot of very intimate details and Mrs. Wilson reciprocates with silence and sound advice. Everyone Has Standards: Outright calls Lord Berbrooke a horrible man for having an illegitimate child with one of his maids and then banishing them both without a penny to their name. Gossipy Hens: She won't spread her employer's secrets, but she's more than happy to make an exception for Lord Berbrooke. Haughty Help: She's not amused at all to find Eloise rummaging through her room and, having been a part of the household since before Eloise was born, has no hesitation in demanding an explanation, social rank be damned.

characters.name: John
characters.description: A Scottish lord whose introverted sensibilities appeal to the newly-debuted Francesca. Big Brother Instinct: While John and Michaela are cousins, they grew up as close as siblings. John insists on respecting Michaela's commitment to spinsterhood, strenuously objecting to Francesca's plan to set Michaela up with men. Doomed by Canon:Considering Francesca's love interest in the books is John's cousin, poor John was doomed not to last long in the show. First Love: Was this to Francesca , understanding , caring and patient.Tragically he dies youngearly into their marriage, just as he and Francesca are at their happiest. Foil: His ardent support of Michaela in her spinsterhood foils Violet's inability to accept Eloise's.

characters.name: Rose
characters.description: Daphne's ladies' maid and friend. The Confidant: Rose is often a listening ear for Daphne, reassuring her about her marriage to Simon, joking around about the Duke and Duchess's "activities," and is the one to finally give DaphneThe Talkwhen she asks. Undying Loyalty: To Daphne. Rose managed to get her mistress out of her marriage to Lord Berbrooke by getting gossip from one of his maids, and even moves out to Clyvedon once Daphne becomes Duchess of Hastings.

characters.name: The Crabtrees
characters.description: The elderly caretakers of Benedict's cottage in the country. Kindly Housekeeper: Definitely in the case of Mr. Crabtree. Mrs. Crabtree is more downplayed, as she has known Benedict since he was little and has no problem scolding him for impropriety, but the moment she learns of Sophie's ordeal with the Cavenders, she has absolutely no problems with treating her as a guest. Old Retainer: Mrs Crabtree has been working for the Bridgertons since she was a young woman. She started out as a maid, and is now a caretaker of one of their properties along with her husband.

characters.name: Hazel
characters.description: A maid in the Bridgerton household who becomes friends with Sophie. Disabled Character, Disabled Actor: GracieMcGonigalwas born without a fully developed left hand in real life. Near-Rape Experience: Philip Cavender and his friends corner her while drunk one night. Sophie gets her away before anything can happen and Benedict backs Sophie up, then makes sure she's safely employed in the Bridgerton household. Phony Psychic: She convinces some of the other servants she can see the future as a joke. Shipper on Deck: Hazel is very invested in Sophie's burgeoning romance.

characters.name: Simon
characters.description: The dashing Duke of Hastings, an eligible bachelor with a dark past. He's an old friend of Anthony's and strikes up a fake courtship with Daphne in the first season. Adaptational Nice Guy: Show Simon is more approachable and social, but still snarky, while book Simon is more mysterious, aloof and closed-off. When his wife, Daphne, decides to no longer sleep with him after discovering his lies about his ability to have children, show Simon just complies while book-Simon threatens her with sexual assault claiming that he "owns" her. All Girls Want Bad Boys: With Daphne.She turns down the pleasant, angst-free Prince for him. Berserk Button: When Nigel taunts him by bringing up his father, he punches Nigel until he's heavily wounded. Best Friends-in-Law: With Anthony, althoughit was a rocky start. They start out as best friends, Anthony disapproves of his relationship with Daphne, Simon and Daphne marry, and Anthony and Simon reconcile by the season's end.

characters.name: The Duke and Duchess of Hastings
characters.description: Simon's deceased parents. Abusive Parents: Simon's father was a perfectionist who was obsessed with his legacy and continuing the Hastings name. He disowned Simon for having a speech impediment as a child, causing Simon a lifetime of emotional issues. Daphne surmises that Simon doesn't think he deserves love unless he's perfect. Deceased Parents Are the Best: Simon's mother was by all accounts a lovely woman and an excellent duchess. Naturally, she died in childbirth and Simon was left to be raised by his abusive father. While he is also dead, it happened a short time before the start of the story and is why Simon is back in town. Death by Childbirth: Simon's mother died after giving birth to him, as shown in a flashback at the beginning of the second episode. Gone Horribly Right: The Duke's horrible treatment of his son did inadvertently give Simon the resolve to overcome his speech impediment; but by the time the Duke's on his deathbed Simon hates his father so much he swears he'llnevermarry or have children, and the Hastings line will end with him.

characters.name: Lady Danbury
characters.description: An established lady in the Ton with a quick wit, discerning eye and cantankerous personality. She is a family friend to the Bridgertons, as well as Duke Simon Basset's surrogate mother, sponsor to the Sharmas and perhaps the only person whom Queen Charlotte sees as an equal. Classy Cane: She's aGrand Damewho uses a cane due to necessity, as her advanced age also has weakened her knees. She's also not above using it as a whacking stick when the need arises... Cool Old Lady: Oh my, yes. She's acerbic and snarky, but while not exactly warm, clearly cares deeply for Simon, the Bridgertons, the Sharmas, and the Mondriches. She's also a mischievous so-and-so who delights in pranking people. She also throws a boisterous party for the married women only and tells Daphne, "Welcome to my den of iniquity." She laments that mature women are unable to express their desires, despite having refined and passionate experience owing to her age, and encourages Violet to express her sexuality. Dare to Be Badass: She basically said this to a young Simon, telling him she'd help him reach his full potential, but it's ultimately up to him. He rose to the challenge, tenfold. Deadpan Snarker: So well-known for this that some of the Bridgertons eliminated her as a Lady Whistledown suspect because she would rather snark at peopleto their faces.

characters.name: Marcus
characters.description: Lady Danbury's brother; he returns to London in season 3. The Charmer: He'sverysmooth, and has the voice to match. He has Lady Danbury's servants in stiches from his witty stories, and can reduce Violet to incoherent mumbling with just the offer of a dance. Chivalrous Pervert: Lady Danbury makes it clear she considers him a rake, and he's certainlya charmer, but he's also incredibly respectful of Violet throughout their courtship. Despite his obvious attraction for her, he repeatedly offers to take things as slow as she wants until she's the one to initiate their intimacy. Mr. Fanservice: When he finally gets intimate with Violet in "An Offer From A Gentleman", he strips down until he's fully nude. Nice Guy: He may have had his issues with his sister, but when it comes to Violet he's courteous, kind, and respects both her desire to take their courtship slow and to keep things discreet around her children.

characters.name: Archibald
characters.description: The aloof and disinterested patriarch of the Featheringtons. He's unusually unconcerned with his daughters' formal coming out into society. The Gambling Addict: Lord Featherington's gambling habit puts his family in dire financial straits. Hoist by His Own Petard:His blatant behaviour during the boxing match clues the bookies that he's rigged the fight, and leads to his death. Inelegant Blubbering: When confronted by his wife about his gambling debts, he collapses into sobbing and blubbering. Killed Offscreen:When he finally lost the gamble, it is implied that he is murdered by the men he'd placed the bet with, Reggie and Tom. After he is invited into a room by those two men, it cuts to the scene where his family is informed about his death.

characters.name: Portia
characters.description: The controlling and somewhat unscrupulous matriarch of the Featheringtons. Insists on her daughters' theme clothing, and is highly protective against threats and proactive during their debut. Anti-Education Mama:She is utterly opposed to her daughters putting effort into anything that does not directly relate to attracting suitors. She outright tells Penelope to stop reading lest it "confuse your thoughts". But, at the same time, her girls are considerably less polished than the Bridgerton daughters, implying that she has not put as much emphasis on formal deportment training either and this ironically makes them less likely to attract suitors since there is little to make them shine in comparison to other debutantes.In the first half of season 3, we find out this lack of instruction extended tothe most basic aspects of intercourse and pregnancy. While Violet didn't teach Daphne these things out of shame and discomfort, it seems Portia just expected Prudence and Philippa to know or have found out these things on their own. But, at the same time, her girls are considerably less polished than the Bridgerton daughters, implying that she has not put as much emphasis on formal deportment training either and this ironically makes them less likely to attract suitors since there is little to make them shine in comparison to other debutantes. While Violet didn't teach Daphne these things out of shame and discomfort, it seems Portia just expected Prudence and Philippa to know or have found out these things on their own. Consistent Clothing Style: She puts herself and all her daughters in color-coded floral dresses.

characters.name: Penelope
characters.description: The ignored Featherington, fast friends with Eloise, and holds a deep abiding crush on Colin. She's far smarter and more observant than given credit for, and willing to put her values over seeming propriety. She is the central character of the third season, as it revolves around her two longest-running plot points: her attraction to Colin, andthe fact that she is the gossip columnist who goes by "Lady Whistledown". Adaptational Attractiveness: In the books, Penelope has difficulty finding suitors, going through ten seasons before marrying at 28, at which point she is considered aMaiden Auntand most suitors had moved onto her younger sister. In the show, she is only about 19 and in her third season by season 3, bringing her more in line with the standards of the time period. Additionally, since she's played by the beautiful Nicola Coughlan, she finds suitors once she gains more confidence and dresses herself in more flattering outfits. That said, the trope is defied in one specific way: in the books, her glow-up coincides with losing some 2 stone in weight (28 lb / 12 kg), whereas Coughlan's is solely via better hairstyles and more flattering clothing. Adaptational Timespan Change: A whole decade passes in the books beforePenelope and Colinmarry, at which point Penelope is 28. The show not only cuts this time jump but moves their story up, meaning Penelope is only about 19 at that point in the show. Adaptational Villainy: In the books, Lady Whistledown is treated as basically harmless, and several characters are even gleeful at the prospect of appearing in her column. However, her actions in the show (particularly regarding Marina) prove that a professional gossip columnist can cause serious harm, especially to women in a society where reputation is everything. Her book version mostly comments on fashion and gossip she's overheard, rather than leaking personal information she was trusted with. Affectionate Nickname: Her closest friends, Colin and Eloise, call her "Pe

characters.name: Prudence and Philippa
characters.description: Penelope's two older sisters, who are both vain, dimwitted and somewhat callous. By season 3, both are married, but remain frequent presences in their mother's and younger sister's lives. Ascended Extra: Prudence gets more screen time in season 2 through the hefty Featherington subplot as her motheralmost marries her off to cousin Jack. The Bus Came Back: Phillipa makes a brief return in season 4. Character Development: In season 3, airhead Philippa wants to become the mother of the new Lord Featherington so she can "get rid of all those dusty books". At the end of the season, inspired by newfound respect for Penelope, she hopes her baby daughter might grow up to be a successful writer. Cloudcuckoolander: Philippa insist on there being "bugs" in the ball they are hosting much to Prudence's bewilderment. At a climactic moment she yells for Varney to release them— and she opens up a cage full of butterflies. Prudence notes Philippa is a genius, and she note's that yeah, they're "bugs."

characters.name: Marina
characters.description: A cousin of the Featheringtons, come to visit to debut in society in search of a husband. At first the most popular girl in the household (much to Portia's jealousy), it's revealed she's actually carrying a scandalous secret. Abled in the Adaptation: Thus far. In the books, Eloise remembers Marina had symptoms of what readers can identify as clinical depression when they were children. Time will tell whether she shows symptoms in later seasons. Adaptational Backstory Change: In the books, she is a distant Bridgerton cousin, but in the series she is a distant Featherington cousin. Adaptational Villainy: Her attempt to trick Colin into marriage does not occur in the books. Ascended Extra: In the books, she's only mentioned postmortem at the beginning of the fifth book. Here she's retooled into a Featherington cousin with her own subplot.

characters.name: Jack
characters.description: The new Featherington heir in season 2. Canon Foreigner: He is a character original for the show adaptation to expand the Featherington plot. Gold Digger:He pursues Cressida Cowper so he can use her dowry to support himself and the Featheringtons. Likes Older Women:Jack pursues Cressida for her money and is willing to marry Prudence to avoid scandal, but the only woman he's shown sincerely attracted to is Portia. He seems genuinely hurt when she stabs him in the back to protect her daughters. Mock Millionaire:He kept up appearances of a man who made a fortune off gemstone mines in America, but the mines he had invested in were empty. He planned on marrying Cressida to bring money into the family, but Portia's scheming put a stop to that.

characters.name: Varley
characters.description: The Featherington housekeeper. Everyone Has Standards:Nasty piece of work she might be, but she's shocked when Mrs. Wilson tells her that Lord Berbrooke got one of his maids pregnant before firing her and sending her off with nothing to support her or the unborn child.She's also horrified when she realises she's unintentionally helped Araminta Penwood put an innocent maid in jail for a crime she didn't commit, and goes behind her employers' back to get help getting her out. Her intervention is what leads to Violet and Benedict arriving in time to prevent Sophie's sentencing. Nasty piece of work she might be, but she's shocked when Mrs. Wilson tells her that Lord Berbrooke got one of his maids pregnant before firing her and sending her off with nothing to support her or the unborn child. She's also horrified when she realises she's unintentionally helped Araminta Penwood put an innocent maid in jail for a crime she didn't commit, and goes behind her employers' back to get help getting her out. Her intervention is what leads to Violet and Benedict arriving in time to prevent Sophie's sentencing. Gossipy Hens: Engages in a bit of this with the Bridgerton housekeeper Mrs. Wilson in the second episode.

characters.name: Harry and Albie
characters.description: Best Friends-in-Law: They are quite close to each other and to Colin. Season 4 shows that they have a regular cheese club together! Birds of a Feather: Like Philippa, Albion is sweet, none-too-bright, and loves cheese. Brainless Beauty: Upon learning that Harry doesn't really have any idea how babymaking works, Portia comments that he is so very...pretty. Decomposite Character: Albion appears to have been created from what once was Lord Berbrooke, a bumbling-but-harmless fellow who would eventually marry Phillipa, while all the television version of Lord Berbrooke inherits from his book counterpart is his unsuccesful pursuit of Daphne Bridgerton. Endearingly Dorky: Neither are the most glamorous or sophisticated of gentlemen but are likeably earnest.

characters.name: Cressida
characters.description: An ill-mannered debutante. Adaptational Sympathy: In the books, Cressida's nothing more than anAlpha Bitchwho exits the narrative after fulfilling her purpose in Daphne and Penelope's stories. Season 3 gives Cressida aFreudian Excusefor her behavior due to mistreatment by her father and a potentialforced marriageto a controlling andfun-hatingelderly man named Lord Greer, which she is miserable about, due to being unable to find a husband herself. We also see more emotional layers to her in her new friendship with Eloise. Alpha Bitch: She not only tries her best to undermine Daphne but also bullies Penelope. Arc Villain: After being a typical mean girl and a nuisance at best in Seasons 1 and 2, Cressida takes over as the main antagonist of Season 3. Arch-Enemy: She is a generally unpleasant person but she's particularly cruel towards Penelope. She goes from a mere nuisance to a main antagonist in Penelope's season, even trying to steal Lady Whistledown from her.

characters.name: Lord and Lady Cowper
characters.description: Cressida's parents who are desperate to get their daughter married off. Abusive Parents: Both:Definitely in the case of Lord Cowper. He is very overbearing and controlling of his daughter, and seems completely unconcerned with her feelings or well-being as long as his reputation is intact. He intended to marry her off to a man old enough to be her great-grandfather when she failed to find a husband on her own, and when she impersonated Lady Whistledown, he was so enraged that he pulled her dowry all together and shipped her off to live with his sister in Wales so she would not embarrass him further.Less in the case of Lady Cowper, but definitely still there. Though she does genuinely want to help her daughter and even goes along with her scheme to impersonate Lady Whistledown, she often gives Cressida backhanded compliments about her failure to find suitors, and refuses to intervene with her husband's wrath when he sends Cressida away. Definitely in the case of Lord Cowper. He is very overbearing and controlling of his daughter, and seems completely unconcerned with her feelings or well-being as long as his reputation is intact. He intended to marry her off to a man old enough to be her great-grandfather when she failed to find a husband on her own, and when she impersonated Lady Whistledown, he was so enraged that he pulled her dowry all together and shipped her off to live with his sister in Wales so she would not embarrass him further. Less in the case of Lady Cowper, but definitely still there. Though she does genuinely want to help her daughter and even goes along with her scheme to impersonate Lady Whistledown, she often gives Cressida backhanded compliments about her failure to find suitors, and refuses to intervene with her husband's wrath when he sends Cressida away. Kick the Dog: Lady Cowper takes full advantage of her daughter's impersonation scheme of Lady Whistledown, going as far as to write nasty things about the Bridgertons for no other reason than f

characters.name: Kate
characters.description: The older Sharma sister and heroine of season 2. Independent and spirited, she aims to find a good husband for her sister, Edwina. Adaptational Attractiveness: Book Kate is not considered as beautiful as Edwina and is insecure about her appearance. The show does not try to pretend Simone Ashley isn't beautiful. Instead, she is styled in the early episodes to reflect her stoic nature, older age, lower birth, and refusal to put herself out there, which makes her less desirable. Adaptational Nationality: In the book, the Sheffields are from Somerset. In the show, Kate is Indian-born and raised at court with an English stepmother. Adaptational Personality Change: Show Kate is famously bold, outspoken and snarky, while book Kate is more passive and insecure. Despite show Kate still having insecurities, they're more about feeling worthy of love rather than her physical appearance — a necessary change given that her actress, Simone Ashley, is absolutely drop-dead gorgeous and therefore Kate worrying about her appearance would be patently ridiculous. Adaptation Name Change: Like the rest of her family her surname goes from Sheffield to Sharma. The Sheffields in the show are Mary's parents. Unlike Mary and Edwina, Kate's first name also changes; "Kate" is now short for Kathani instead of Katharine.

characters.name: Edwina
characters.description: The younger Sharma sister, a genteel young lady immediately dubbed the diamond of the season. Adaptational Dumbass: In the book, she claims to have always known Anthony and Kate would end up together. In the show, she's completely oblivious until the last minute. Beware the Nice Ones: Having been raised to be aProper Ladysince she was a child, she's a friendly and sweet young woman. However, when pressed to her breaking point, she's fully capable of a scathing"The Reason You Suck" Speechand leaving the person who wronged her burned with shame. Anthony and Kate realize this when Edwina realizes their suppressed feelings for one anotheron her wedding day at the altarand how they've been lying to her. Anthony remarks how Edwina proved "harsher" than he thought her capable of. Blame the Paramour: After theaborted wedding, she displays far more anger towards Kate than she ever does to Anthony beyond some generalcoldness. This could be justified by the fact that she is much closer to Kate and trusts her while she barely knows Anthony, thus she feels the betrayal from Kate more deeply. Character Development: She goes from being almost totally dependent on her sister and mother to realizing she wants to become her own woman who has her own thoughts, opinions, and is capable of independence.

characters.name: Mary
characters.description: Edwina's mother and Kate's stepmother, a former noblewoman whose marriage to a clerk caused a scandal in the town. Because You Were Nice to Me: The reason why Kate willingly took over her late dad's role at the expense of her own desires and happiness, was because Kate owes so much to Mary for taking her in. However, when Kate actually voices this belief to Mary, Mary immediately says that Kate doesn't owe her a thing; Mary considers Kate her own daughter, and it was never a question as to whether she'd treat her as such. Good Stepmother: She considers her stepdaughter Kate her own and states this when her parents say they have onlyonegrandchild from her; immediately correcting that she hastwodaughters. Mary feels guilty to not be able to give a season to Kate, but accepts Kate's content with the latter's life choice. When Kate confesses to believing that she owed her so much for taking her in during the finale, Mary tells Kate that sheneverhad to earn her love, because the moment they met, she already had considered Kate herown.Lady Sheffield:She simply sailed away from all of us with that man, robbing us of our grandchild!Mary:Grandchildren. I havetwodaughters, with whom you have had every opportunity to form a connection with, but the choice to shun us was yours alone. Impoverished Patrician: She was born a nobleman's daughter, but married a working-class man. The money dried up after he died and she's now come to London hoping that her daughter can marry well. Marry for Love: Prior to the events, despite she was a season's Incomparable and desired by many noble suitors, nevertheless she adamantly chose to marry a working-class royal clerk, Mr. Sharma, out of genuine love, much to her parents' fury and cue the scandal.

characters.name: Lord and Lady Sheffield
characters.description: An Earl and his wife, and the parents of Mary Sharma. Gruesome Grandparent: They effectively disowned their daughter Mary after the shame brought about by herInter-Class Romance, and are cold to Edwina (Mary's biological daughter) and (especially) Kate (Edwina's stepsister). Because of their classism, they refuse to acknowledge Kate as a member of the family and will only formally acknowledge and support Edwina if she makes a suitably high society marriage. Anthony reasonably acknowledges their toxicity and tells them to eat dirt. I Have No Daughter!: They immediately disowned their daughter, Mary, for going against them by marrying a commoner out of love, instead of their chosen nobleman. Jerkass: They spend their entire screentime badmouthing the Sharmas' presence of Anthony and his mother until Mary finally snaps, and even openly admit to Kate's secret of having Edwina marry a noble to secure the Sheffield's inheritance. It's so much so that, despite being upset about Kate's deception, Anthony openly tells them it was their attitude, and not the shame of their daughter running away, what shun them from society, and makes it clear in no uncertain terms they are not invited to his wedding with Edwina. Nobility Marries Money: Their life principle. They set a match for Mary with an Earl who owned 12.000 acres, but Mary declined said match in favor of marrying a commoner royal clerk, Mr. Sharma, out of genuine love. Much to their anger and cue the scandal.

characters.name: Michaela
characters.description: Artistic License – History: The name Michaela was neither recorded in Britain nor other Anglophone countries until the 20th-century. Closet Key: Appears to be this forFrancesca, who had showed no interest in women previously but is rendered agaping,stammeringmess upon meeting Michaela for the first time. Michaela is aGender Flipof Michael Stirling, who was theLove InterestofFrancescain her book. Gender Flip: She is based on the book character Michael Stirling. Promotion to Opening Titles: After her brief introduction in the season 3 finale, Michaela is upgraded to a main character. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: She clandestinely flees London afterJohn's funeral, for reasons that are yet to be revealed.

characters.name: Will
characters.description: Simon's old friend, a boxer. Bromantic Foil: One of Simon's best friends, and a source of advice and contrast. Unlike the rich, single Simon, Will is a working-class family man. Family Man: Unlike Simon, he's got a wife and kids to worry about, and they prove to be his motivation throughout the show. Happily Married: He and his wife, Alice, seem to be happily married as they're seen to always support each other and rarely argue. Honor Before Reason: Despite knowing doing so would ruin his reputation,Will cannot stand by and allow the new Lord Featherington to con his customers, and exposes him. Fortunately, Benedict and Colin ensure his clientele is not just secured, but expanded, as a reward for his honesty.

characters.name: Alice
characters.description: Will's supportive wife. Ascended Extra: She is a tertiary character in the first two seasons, but becomes a more important supporting character in the third afterher distant aunt bequeaths her title to Alice's son, and Alice begins to adjust to her new status. Lady in Waiting: Becoming the mother of a baron gives her enough social status to become one of Queen Charlotte's ladies (of course, Lady Danbury also pushes for it). She wants to use her position to help better society. Promotion to Opening Titles: Alice becomes a main character in season 4. Secret-Keeper:She knows about Benedict and Sophie's affair, but she decides to keep it to herself. Later, she discusses it with her husband and with her husband's support, she sets up for the Queen to witness the Bridgertons and the Penwoods' meeting for Sophie's status validation.

characters.name: Sophie
characters.description: The illegitimate daughter of the Earl of Penwood. The heroine of season 4, she forms an attachment with Benedict Bridgerton. Adaptational Dye-Job: Was a dark blonde in the books, but is played by the black-haired Yerin Ha. Bastard Angst: She is the illegitimate daughter of an earl. Her father gave her a lady's education while he was alive, but she has little protection or social status after his death and her stepmother treats her as a servant. It's also why she doesn't see herself as a legitimate prospect for Benedict, who is the second son of a viscount. Brainy Brunette: Sophie has long, dark hair and is noticably well-educated, having read extensively and speaking several languages, with Eloise mentioning knowledge of arts and science as well. She also posseses plenty of practical skills her upper-classmen aren't aware of, such as using kindling to light a fire and using alcohol to treat and dress an infected wound. Clark Kenting: Nobody recognises Sophie as the Lady in Silver at the masquerade ball. Justified in that no one would consider a maid a candidate; it doesn't occur in people's minds as a possibility. She also has the advantage of a much more substantial mask than most of the partygoers.

characters.name: Araminta
characters.description: The widowed Countess of Penwood, mother to Rosamund and Posy and stepmother to Sophie. Absurdly Youthful Mother: Although Araminta's age is not stated, shelooksyoung enough to be her daughters' sister.noteKatie Leung was 37 during the filming of Season 4, and is only a year or two older than some of the Bridgerton siblings' actors and only a decade older than the actress of Araminta's eldest daughter. Abusive Parents:When Lord Penwood dies and seemingly leaves Sophie out of his will, she manipulates Sophie into staying as her maid in exchange for "protection". She spends years treating Sophie as a virtual slave and forcing her to do the work of four maids without pay. When she discovers that Sophie sneaked into the masquerade ball, she kicks Sophie out without pay or references, and even spreads rumors to ensure that Sophie wouldn't be able to find work again. A flashback shows that she treated Sophie cruelly even when Lord Penwood was alive, forcing Sophie out of a dancing lesson with her daughters.She is also very dismissive of her younger daughter, Posy, heaping all her praise and attention on Rosamund instead. When Lord Penwood dies and seemingly leaves Sophie out of his will, she manipulates Sophie into staying as her maid in exchange for "protection". She spends years treating Sophie as a virtual slave and forcing her to do the work of four maids without pay. When she discovers that Sophie sneaked into the masquerade ball, she kicks Sophie out without pay or references, and even spreads rumors to ensure that Sophie wouldn't be able to find work again. A flashback shows that she treated Sophie cruelly even when Lord Penwood was alive, forcing Sophie out of a dancing lesson with her daughters. She is also very dismissive of her younger daughter, Posy, heaping all her praise and attention on Rosamund instead.

characters.name: Rosamund
characters.description: Araminta's eldest daughter, the vain and spoiled one. Adaptational Dye-Job: Was blonde in the books, but is played by the dark-haired Michelle Mao. Adaptational Name Change: Her surname was Reiling in the books, but is Li in the show. Big Sister Bully: She regularly belittles Posy for her talkative nature and for her kindness towards Sophie. The Dragon: To her mother; Rosamund is the secondary antagonist of Season 4, even described by Jess Brownwell as one of the franchise's biggest villains.

characters.name: Posy
characters.description: Araminta's younger daughter, who is sweet and kind but chatty. Adaptational Attractiveness: Book Posy gets appearance-shamed by her own mother and negatively compared to Rosamund. Isabella Wei is just as conventionally pretty as her onscreen sister. Adaptational Name Change: Her surname was Reiling in the books, but is Li in the show. Adaptational Slimness: Book Posy is described as chubby, whereas she is thin onscreen. Big Little Sister: She's the younger sibling, but she's taller than her older sister, Rosamund.

characters.name: Irma Gibbons
characters.description: The no-nonsense cook of the Penwood household, who's had to develop a tough skin to cope with the whims of her employer but nonetheless has a soft spot for Sophie. Composite Character: Of both Cinderella's Fairy Godmother and her mice friends. She's one of Sophie's closest confidents and friends, and helps her sneak into the Masquerade Ball. Small Role, Big Impact: Had she and Alfie had not convinced Sophie to go to the Masquerade ball, Benedict and Sophie never would have met. She reappears in the last episode to help Sophie and Alfie look for the Penwood will, uncovering the real reason Araminta kept Sophie and thatSophie has a dowry.

characters.name: Alfie
characters.description: A sarcastic and witty footman who's always ready to come to Sophie's defense. Ambiguously Bi: OrAmbiguously Gay. He makes jokes about having seen ladies in their underwear before, suggesting some sexual experience with women; however when making a throwaway comment about Sophie's hypothetical duty as Benedict's mistress of keeping Benedict happy, he remarks that this "would probably please you... it would certainly please me". Composite Character: Of both Cinderella'sFairy Godmotherand her mice friends. He's one of Sophie's closest confidents and friends, and helps her sneak into the Masquerade Ball. Give Away the Bride:He walks Sophie down the aisle at her wedding in the post-credits scene. Shipper on Deck: For Sophie and Benedict. When Benedict calls on Penwood house, he encourages Sophie to tell him that she's the Lady in Silver he's been searching for, believing that Benedict will take Sophie away from her abusive family once he learns the truth. He's more positive about Benedict's offer to Sophie to be his mistress, although he doesn't push Sophie to accept it, merely asking her reasons for her rejection and accepting her answer.

characters.name: Richard
characters.description: Sophie's biological father, the deceased Earl of Penwood. Adaptational Nice Guy: Downplayed; both versions take Sophie as his ward and have her raised as a young lady. However, in the book he is still distant towards Sophie. Here, he is more doting on her in private and promised to always make sure she would be taken care of. Deceased Parents Are the Best: Though he never publicly claimed Sophie as his daughter, it's clear he doted on her. He gave her a lady's educationand a respectable dowry. So of course, he bites it and Sophie'sWicked Stepmothertakes over her rearing. Hanky-Panky with the Help: He had Sophie through an affair with a maid. Horrible Judge of Character: To say the least, he severely misapprehended Araminta's suitability as a mother figure for Sophie.

characters.name: New Lord Penwood
characters.description: Living Prop: He exists as a way to get Cressida a husband that she is overall content with and drive Araminta and her daughters out of Penwood House. He doesn't get a first name, much in the way of personality, or a line.

characters.name: Queen Charlotte
characters.description: The haughty, mercurial and judgmental queen of England, whose marriage to King George III opened the doors to racial equality in the setting. She presides over the ton every season. She is also the protagonist of the spinoffQueen Charlotte: A Bridgerton Story. Affectionate Nickname: Her husband, George, calls her Lottie whenever he is in normal state. Became Their Own Antithesis: As a young woman, she was headstrong and rebellious, actively resenting herArranged Marriagewith George (at least until she met him), her position as Queen and her duty as aBaby Factory. By the time she enters her twilight years, she has become the very apex of English high society and forces several of her children into arranged marriages of their own to produce a legitimate child that can succeed the crown. Beneath the Mask: She's very haughty in public, but her private life is pointedly not perfect, as her husband is senile. Especially poignant because she clearly does love George dearly, and it breaks her heart to see his mind disintegrate before her.

characters.name: Lord Berbrooke
characters.description: An unattractive suitor who hopes to gain Daphne's hand. Abhorrent Admirer: He's initially an acceptable suitor by Anthony's standards, but Daphne is appalled by him and emphatically declares she will never marry him. She's even less enchanted when he tries to force himself onto her. Adaptational Villainy: In the books he is portrayed as a bumbling fool, not a villain. Boisterous Weakling: Nigel tries to square up to Simon, who ignores him up until he insults Daphne and thenbrings up the late Duke of Hastings, which unsurprisingly earns him a swiftNo-Holds-Barred Beatdown. Deliberate Values Dissonance: Berbrooke is the embodiment of the Regency Era attitude that women were little more thantrade goods, to be bought and sold between families for financial and (essentially) breeding purposes. He even compares her to ahorse. Admittedly, he's such a heartless example of this that even other lords and nobility find his opinions odious.

characters.name: Friedrich
characters.description: A Prussian prince and the Queen's nephew, who comes to London looking for a bride. Betty and Veronica: He's thenice,charming, good-husband-material Betty to Simon's Veronica for Daphne's Archie. Historical Domain Character: The show's version ofPrince Frederick Wilhelm Ludwig. Graceful Loser: Refuses to "fight" for Daphne as his aunt encourages, knowing that she's clearly happy with Simon and it's not his place to ruin that. I Kiss Your Hand: Prince Friedrich kisses Cressida Cowper's hand at one event. Daphne and Simon muse about how it's a calculated flirtation strategy.

characters.name: Lord Debling
characters.description: A lord with a passion for nature. He enters the marriage market in season 3. Lord Debling is an individualist and is considered an oddball among society, but nonetheless remains a desirable prospect for young ladies. Birds of a Feather: Forms a connection with Penelope based on being the black sheep of their respective families, and their preference for intellectual independence rather than following societal expectations. Canon Foreigner: He does not exist in the books. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: He disappears in season 3 part 2 after his courtship with Penelope falls apart, and it's unknown whether he ended up marrying or to whom. Doomed by Canon: Not him, but assuming that the show follows real life in this regard, his crusade to save the great auk from extinction.

characters.name: Lady Arnold
characters.description: A lady who has made the most of being a wealthy widow. Everyone Is Bi: She seems to hold this philosophy to an extent, at least the idea that attraction is not limited by gender, and discusses it with Benedict. Fiction Isn't Fair: She might be a widow, thus no longer held to the standards of a debutante, and intentionally portrayed as ahead of her time, but it still wouldn't be considered appropriate for even the most liberated Regency widows to kiss a man she is not married to in public. Friends with Benefits: She initially makes it clear to Benedict as they enter a sexual relationship that she has no intention of being wooed or remarrying. However, shechanges her mindand wants pursue him more seriously just as Benedict decides he's not ready to settle down. Genre Refugee: From her Old Hollywood-esque glam dresses and hair to the way she behaves, she seemsout of place in the Regency periodeven in the increasingly anachronistic season 3, like she stepped out of a time machine from the next century.

characters.name: Lord Barnaby
characters.description: A kind nobleman who forms an attraction with Posy Li. Composite Character: Has elements of Hugh Woodson, Posy's love interest in the books, such as his kind nature, bright smile, and attentive listening to Posy's stories. Foil: To Lord Stotter, Rosamund's suitor. While Stotter was a fortune hunter who terminated his engagement with Rosamund upon learning her dowry was not as large as he thought, Barnaby is genuinely interested in Posy as a person and their attraction is genuine. If you look closely at the ending of "Dance in the Country", Posy is wearing an engagement ring. How They Treat the Help: Is perfectly happy to sit with the staff of Bridgerton and Penwood House at Sophie and Benedict's wedding, as part of Sophie's wedding party. Nice Guy: A sweet, mild-mannered gentleman who falls head over heels for Posy and always listens to her ramblings. At Benedict and Sophie's wedding, he smiles widely and brightly.

characters.name: Lady Whistledown
characters.description: A mysterious figure who exposes gossip and scandals through her society papers. Beneath Suspicion: Eloise figures that Whistledown must somehow be privy to important gossip and events but isn't important enough to be noticed. Broken Pedestal: Eloise admires Whistledown's speaking truth to power and independence, though she does wish Whistledown would stop causing trouble for her and her loved ones.The admiration goes kaput when she finds out Whistledown is actually her best friend Penelope. Eloise promptly ends their friendship. Character Narrator: Lady Whistledown narrates the show through voiceovers describing events. However, she also exists as a figure within the show, and Eloise and the Queen strive to uncover her identity. Expy: Of the eponymousGossip Girl. She serves the same role for the narrative as Gossip Girl, she causes similar problems for the cast, and her identity is hidden from the audience in the same way.

characters.name: Brimsley
characters.description: Queen Charlotte's unflappable butler and right-hand man. The Confidant: Privy to more information than most courtiers will hear in a lifetime. Consummate Professional: Treats his duties with utmost seriousness even when it's just investigating court gossip. Everyone Has Standards: Despite hisUndying Loyaltyto Queen Charlotte, not even Brimsley can bring himself to say that she's been a good mother to her children. When Charlotte point-blank asks him about her parenting skills, he tries his best to talk around his true opinion, instead emphasizing how great aqueenshe's been. Haughty Help: He has no qualms about putting Eloise in her place, despite her far outranking him.

characters.name: Siena
characters.description: Adaptation Name Change: Known as Maria in the books. Ascended Extra: Anthony alludes to a previous relationship with an opera singer; he and Maria have a brief conversation while Kate hides under a desk inThe Viscount who Loved Me. The show gives this relationship screentime throughout the first season. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Siena never appears again after moving on from Anthony in her last appearance. However, she is briefly mentioned by Benedict in season 4 during a conversation with Colin and Mondrich. False Soulmate: While Anthony is certainly attracted to Siena and enjoys the escapism she provides from his duties, they do not have a loving relationship and are not compatible at the end of the day.Word of Godconfirms he didn't love her, and Anthony later calls their time together a "dalliance". Meaningful Name: Her surname means red in Italian, so it matches her signature outfit color.

characters.name: Mme. Delacroix
characters.description: A London dressmaker whom the other characters frequent. She's also a friend of Siena's. As Long as It Sounds Foreign: Has a very unconvincing French accent. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Becomes inexplicably absent in season 4 and isn't even mentioned at all. Everything Sounds Sexier in French: Implied to be the reason she fakes being French — her aristocratic clients are drawn in by the prestige of having a French-accented dressmaker make their clothes.noteFrench-style fashions were very in style in 1810s England. Fauxreigner: The audience learns early in the first season that Madam Delacroix is only pretending to be French. She puts on astereotypical French accentin front of customers, but drops it around friends like Siena.

characters.name: Theo
characters.description: A printer's assistant who Eloise meets during her search for Lady Whistledown. Birds of a Feather: He and Eloise are both bookish, opinionated, and interested in social reform. Canon Foreigner: He doesn't exist in the books. Deadpan Snarker: Frequently sarcastic, especially concerning high society. Interclass Friendship: He's a working-class man who befriends and later falls for lady of the ton Eloise despite their massive difference in status.
